lede: A 3D, broadcast-style replay of the 2026 Sepang weekend. Every practice session, qualifying and the race, rebuilt from public OpenF1 data: real names, positions, telemetry, tyres, race control and weather, with the cars driving an aligned 3D model of the circuit.

facts.label: Data
facts.value: OpenF1 · 2026 Sepang weekend (2 to 4 October) · 5 sessions, 22 cars

facts.label: Stack
facts.value: React 19 · TypeScript · Three.js (React Three Fiber) · Vite · Python · Claude API

sections.headline: Watch the race again, from any seat.

body: Sepang Vision Lab replays the 2026 Sepang weekend in 3D, in the browser. Pick a session, follow any of the 22 cars and switch between five cameras while a timing tower, track map, weather and race-control messages run alongside, the way a television broadcast would show them.

Everything on screen comes from recorded data. Where the data cannot say something, such as track width, brake temperature or the scenery around the circuit, the app either leaves it out or labels it as illustrative.

sections.headline: Public data is sparse and noisy.

body: OpenF1 publishes car positions at about four samples a second, with jittery timestamps, in a coordinate system that matches no map. Tyre stints sometimes contradict the pit stops. Sessions have gaps.

Played back as they arrive, the cars stutter, cut corners, overlap and float above the track. The work was turning that into motion that looks physical without inventing anything the data does not contain.

items.caption: Race, lap 11, under the safety car: the TV camera on Charles Leclerc, the 22-car timing tower, the driver card with live speed, gear, throttle and g-force, and the replay bar with incident markers.
On a phone: one scrolling column with the 3D view, replay controls and the followed driver's telemetry.
Chase camera with the driving HUD: rev arc, gear and g-meter, all from recorded channels.
Inspect camera around a team-style livery. Colours only, no logos.
The pit lane, derived from where cars actually drove during the race's 73 pit stops.

sections.headline: Fetch once, replay in the browser.

value.label: Sepang Vision Lab data flow
value.caption: No backend at runtime. The site is static; the replay files are committed and served from Vercel.

nodes.title: OpenF1 API
nodes.detail: Meeting 1308: laps, positions, telemetry, stints, pits, race control, weather.

nodes.detail: Python, standard library only. Cached, resumable and throttled, then compacted into replay files.

nodes.title: Derive

nodes.title: Replay files
nodes.detail: One file per session and driver, committed to the repo.

nodes.detail: React Three Fiber scene reading the replay clock every frame.

nodes.title: Viewer
nodes.detail: Picks a session, a driver and a camera, scrubs, compares and shares a moment.

sections.headline: Making noisy data move like a car.

items.title: Alignment
items.detail: OpenF1 positions are fitted to the circuit model with a derived similarity transform: 3.09 m RMS and 5.69 m at the 95th percentile from the centre line, a residual that includes the real racing line.

items.title: Smooth motion
items.detail: Each car's distance along the track and its offset across it are refitted with a Gaussian-weighted local fit against time, so cars follow their real line and steer from its curvature.

items.title: Physics check
items.detail: Sampling every car at 50 Hz across the race, 99% of frames stay within 3.7 g braking or acceleration and 5.9 g cornering, the range of a real car.

items.title: Elevation
items.detail: About 22 m of climbs and drops, derived from OpenF1 heights. Cars, cameras, scenery and terrain all follow it.

items.title: Cars keep their space
items.detail: Aligned positions carry a few metres of error, so overlapping cars are eased apart sideways. Overlapping frames in the race fell from 3,955 to 211, and only pairs that race control reports as colliding may touch.

items.title: Honest gaps
items.detail: When OpenF1's tyre labels disagree, the tower shows ? instead of a guess. A data gap holds the last sample and marks the car stale after two seconds.

items.title: Five cameras
items.detail: TV, Chase, Onboard, Heli and Inspect, with a speed-sensitive lens and a driving HUD in Chase and Onboard.

items.title: Compare and share
items.detail: Compare two drivers on the same lap with an optional ghost car, and copy a link that reopens the exact session, moment, driver and camera.

items.title: Weather
items.detail: Rain falls while OpenF1 reports rain, then the track dries over about 90 minutes, a drying time fitted to the race's intermediate stint.

items.title: Race engineer
items.detail: Ask about gaps, tyres, pace or flags and hear the answer as a radio call. Presets are answered from the data with no key. With the viewer's own Anthropic API key, Claude answers anything from the same data brief and is told to use only its numbers.

items.title: Hand gestures
items.detail: Optional webcam control through MediaPipe, running locally: swipe to skip, pinch to follow the next driver. No frames leave the browser.

items.title: Fast first load
items.detail: three.js and MediaPipe are kept out of the first download, which fell from 988 KB to under 300 KB.

sections.headline: Live, and checked against the source.

body: All five sessions were compared with the live OpenF1 API for laps, stints, pits, race control and classification, and the position and telemetry streams have no gap over 60 seconds.

Earlier versions replayed the 2017 Malaysian Grand Prix from timing data, with lap-time models and Monte Carlo strategy tools. Those were removed so the project could focus on doing one recorded weekend well.

items.title: Fix the data before the visuals
items.detail: Most of what looked like rendering bugs, such as stutter, cars overlapping or floating, came from the data. Fixing it at the source fixed every view at once.

items.title: Label every number
items.detail: DERIVED, SOURCED, OFFICIAL or illustrative: saying where each value comes from is what lets a replay be trusted.

items.title: Cut to focus
items.detail: Removing the strategy and ML tools made the product clearer, not smaller.

items.title: Give AI a narrow job
items.detail: The race engineer only answers from a brief of recorded data, so it explains the race without inventing it.
